tasks.corrected_reference_answer: Each Agg canvas caches RendererAgg by width, height and dpi, creating it when the key changes (lib/matplotlib/backends/backend_agg.py:388-395). Figure._get_renderer directly calls canvas.get_renderer when available (lib/matplotlib/figure.py:2849-2852), so repeated legend extent queries do not require prior canvas.draw or trigger full drawing on Agg. The fallback captures a renderer by immediately aborting a patched draw (lib/matplotlib/backend_bases.py:1589-1618). Separate figures have separate caches, but this test does not quantify a performance degradation.

tasks.notes: Direct static review of central mechanism and assumptions, not measured performance.
tasks.corrected_reference_answer: TransformWrapper.set invalidates using the old child state, checks dimensional compatibility, removes the old parent link, attaches the new child and rebinds delegated methods (lib/matplotlib/transforms.py:1743-1771). It then resets _invalid, invalidates with the new child in place, and resets again (lib/matplotlib/transforms.py:1776-1778). invalidate chooses affine-only versus full invalidation from is_affine, rather than copying a child invalid flag (lib/matplotlib/transforms.py:154-176). Thus ancestors are notified around a possible change in transform type while the delegating wrapper ends with _invalid=0.
